strings.name: Michael I. Jordan
strings.summary: Michael I. Jordan connects statistical inference, computation and cognitive science in machine learning. Formerly on the faculties of MIT and UC Berkeley, he is now a Berkeley professor emeritus and a researcher at Inria Paris. With David Blei and Andrew Ng, he introduced latent Dirichlet allocation. He also studies connections between machine learning, economic incentives and collective decisions. He is not the basketball player of the same name.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026: selected education, appointments, publications and public activities. Award editions are distinguished from ceremony dates. Personal records disagree on the Inria start year, so it is not assigned a definite timeline entry.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced machine learning, probabilistic modeling and statistical inference, linking computer science with methods for large-scale data analysis.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth
strings.facts.f1.value: Born February 25, 1956 in Aberdeen, Maryland, United States, according to the IEEE award-recipient Q&A.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BS in psychology, Louisiana State University (1978); MS in mathematics, Arizona State University (1980); PhD in cognitive science, UC San Diego (1985).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Latent Dirichlet allocation
strings.highlights.h1.text: With David Blei and Andrew Ng, introduced LDA, using probabilistic topic mixtures to represent discrete data such as documents.
strings.highlights.h2.title: An economic perspective on machine learning
strings.highlights.h2.text: Advocates studying AI in social and market settings, including incentives, creator compensation and collective decisions; these are his research interests and views.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Appears on the INFORMS podcast
strings.timeline.t1.text: The society releases his interview about links between machine learning, statistics, computation and decisions; the date is the episode release date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Receives the Frontiers of Knowledge Award
strings.timeline.t2.text: Shares the 17th Information and Communication Technologies award with Anil Jain and gives an acceptance speech; the edition is labeled 2024.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes professor emeritus at Berkeley
strings.timeline.t3.text: Ends the regular professorship begun in 1998, becomes emeritus and continues his research.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-publishes the LDA paper
strings.timeline.t4.text: Publishes latent Dirichlet allocation with David Blei and Andrew Ng in JMLR, presenting a method for modeling document topics.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joins the Berkeley faculty
strings.timeline.t5.text: Becomes a professor in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences and in Statistics.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Begins teaching at MIT
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joins Brain and Cognitive Sciences as an assistant professor, later earns promotions, and remains until 1998.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earns a cognitive science doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completes his PhD at UC San Diego.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes undergraduate psychology
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduates magna cum laude with a BS in psychology from Louisiana State University.
